quantifiers.original: For every T choose one generator bound valid for all t≤T and w. For every nonnegative t choose an integrable centered Z and an a.e. event. The conclusions cover every pair a,b and each finite T.
quantifiers.reconstructed: The identical order and scope of C, residual, event and endpoint quantifiers.

assumptions.original: Joint measurability of X and A, continuous g, local pointwise uniform state bound and centered increment condition.
assumptions.reconstructed: Same probability, topology, measurability, continuity, bound and residual assumptions.
assumptions.evidence: The source specifies integrals on nonnegative horizons. Using the reconstruction's clamp inside that integral is equivalent because t⁺=t on nonnegative times.

conclusion.original: B locally integrable on ℝ, all signed nonnegative two-time balances, F absolutely continuous on each [0,T], and ordinary F′=B for a.e. positive t.
conclusion.evidence: The printed `HasDerivAt` over `volume.restrict (Ioi 0)` is the stated ordinary a.e. derivative.

scopes.original: Nonnegative endpoints may coincide, be reversed, or include zero. The derivative uses Lebesgue a.e. strictly positive real t.
scopes.reconstructed: Same endpoint and strictly positive a.e. derivative scopes.
scopes.evidence: No pointwise or right derivative at zero, no derivative at every positive time, and no path continuity or martingale premise.

constant_dependencies.original: One pointwise state-uniform bound per finite nonnegative horizon, plus the fixed extension t⁺=max(t,0).
constant_dependencies.evidence: No common rate, global bound, continuity of the generator or multiplicative normalization is imposed.

review_evidence: The complete WeakMeasurableEvolution proof identifies every generator average by pushforward integration, proves measurability by product integration, and obtains local integrability from the horizon bound and the clamped real extension. On each nonnegative horizon, finite product integrability and centering give the base balance. Subtraction produces the signed two-time identity and the horizon bound gives Lipschitz continuity and hence absolute continuity. Lebesgue differentiation applies to the locally integrable primitive, and local equality in an open positive-time neighborhood gives the ordinary derivative.
